key_insight: Vacancy loops in irradiated tungsten evolve differently depending on geometry and orientation: parallel loops can weaken, annihilate, or be transported, while inclined loops react to form strong sessile <100> segments that greatly increase dislocation pinning.
engineering_relevance: These atomistic interaction rules provide constitutive-model inputs for predicting irradiation hardening and defect evolution in fusion reactor tungsten under plastic deformation.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of edge dislocations interacting with vacancy loops in tungsten
Systematic variation of loop size, crystallographic orientation, and dislocation-loop intersection geometry
Translation of atomistic obstacle strengths into mesoscale constitutive parameters
evidence_signal: The study uses simulation-based interaction outcomes across multiple geometries to identify clear differences in defect evolution and pinning strength, especially between parallel and inclined loop configurations.
watch_item: The constitutive mapping is based on atomistic simulations, so transferability to broader irradiation conditions and higher-scale microstructures may require additional validation.
paper_title: Evolution of the Irradiation Induced Defect Landscape through Dislocation Vacancy Loop Interactions in Tungsten
